title: Data Structures with C
goal: Linked lists, stack, queue, BST, hash table aur BFS/DFS ko C me implement karna.
definition: Data structure data ko organize karta hai taaki operations efficient hon: linked list O(1) insert/delete, stack LIFO, queue FIFO, BST O(log n) search (balanced), hash table average O(1).
explain: Singly linked list me node {data, next}; head se traverse; insert/delete me pointers update karo aur free karo. Doubly me prev pointer. Circular me tail next head ko.
Stack LIFO hai — push/pop top par; array ya linked list se. Queue FIFO — enqueue rear, dequeue front; circular array se space reuse.
BST me left < root < right; search/insert/delete average O(log n), worst O(n) (skewed). Traversal inorder sorted order deta hai.
Hash table key ko hash function se index me badalta hai; collision ke liye chaining (linked list) ya open addressing. Load factor badhe to resize.
analogy: Linked list ek treasure hunt hai: har clue agle clue ka address deta hai. Array ek shelf hai jahan index se seedha pahunchte ho — insert ke liye shifting chahiye.
why: Ye structures real systems me hain: undo stack, printer queue, database index (B-tree), cache (hash map), graph traversal. Interviews me linked list reverse aur cycle detection classic hain.

syntax.note: Naya node head ban jaata hai — O(1).

topics.title: Linked lists
topics.body: Singly/doubly/circular; insert head/tail, delete by key, reverse, cycle detection (Floyd), middle (slow/fast). Har node ka free yaad rakho.

topics.title: Stack aur queue
topics.body: Stack: push/pop/peek, balanced parentheses, expression evaluation, undo. Queue: enqueue/dequeue, circular array, BFS. Deque dono ends. Priority queue heap se.

topics.title: Trees aur BST
topics.body: Binary tree traversal preorder/inorder/postorder/level-order. BST search/insert/delete, min/max, height. Balanced trees (AVL/Red-Black) guarantee O(log n).

topics.title: Hash table aur graphs
topics.body: Hash function, chaining, load factor, resize. Graph adjacency list/matrix; BFS queue se shortest unweighted path; DFS stack/recursion se connectivity/cycle.

interview.q: Linked list kab array se better?
interview.a: Jab frequent insert/delete head/middle par ho aur random access ki zaroorat na ho; size dynamic ho. Array cache-friendly aur O(1) indexing deta hai.
interview.followUp: Real use? — LRU cache, adjacency list, undo.

interview.a: Chaining (same bucket me linked list) ya open addressing (linear/quadratic probing, double hashing). Load factor threshold par resize.
interview.followUp: Worst case? — O(n); balanced tree buckets se O(log n).
